maria: Quick sync idea: push a tiny deterministic policy eval into a sidecar to avoid hot-path RPCs. Capturing tradeoffs.
kishore: Define "tiny". What can we safely run locally?
maria: Fast-eval subset: region checks, latency thresholds, tenant-tier flags, simple priority buckets. No price feeds, no heavy arithmetic.
sam: We saw P99 regressions from cross-process lookups. Local eval could shave ~2-8ms on hot path.
elaine: Risks: staleness, rollout churn, capacity imbalance if sidecars diverge.
maria: Proposal: control plane is authoritative. Ship signed versioned deltas. Sidecar runs fast-eval; if unsure, fallback to control plane.
kishore: Deltas: keep monotonic versions. If out-of-order, fetch snapshot. No CRDTs initialy.
sam: Telemetry: annotate traces with policy.eval=sidecar|controlplane and policy.version; emit mismatch logs during mirror-read phase.
elaine: Add TTL guard: if version_age > T, sidecar enters conservative mode (penalize preferences, avoid preemption).
maria: Rollout plan: (1) grammar + signed deltas (2) sidecar SDK + sync (3) mirror-read logging (4) gated canary write.
sam: Tests: deterministic fuzz, network partition chaos, perf target: sidecar eval P50 < 100us.
elaine: Ops: admin endpoint to force snapshot refresh and FF to disable sidecar globally.
maria: Action: kishore draft grammar (EOW), sam prototype sync (next sprint), elaine write rollout checklist (next week).
deploy-bot: deploy request submitted by maria for branch policy-sidecar-proto -> staging (CI: queued)
Maria: I'll write RFC follow-up. Call out missing failure modes here.
